perViewScores.note: The front is closed and entrance-led, but it is a sparse boxy onion-dome fort. The huge black circular entrance/rose assembly, flat wall fields, repeated hemispheres, and pale orange finish do not reproduce the source's compact ornate honey cathedral.

The source-facing facade thins into broad planar slabs, the purple door breaks into a wedge, the circular rose/backplane exposes substantial side depth, and repeated domes replace occupied honeycomb bay masses.
A real side wall exists, but it is a broad under-authored slab with sparse extruded windows, flat purple strips, generic domes, and the front circular feature visible as an oversized disk/paper edge.
The giant front circular backplane protrudes beyond the palace silhouette, and side posts/windows read as loosely attached pieces rather than wrapped structural ribs and occupied bays.

The rear is closed and authored with a subordinate service apse, but it remains a sparse box-and-dome elevation without source-like honeycomb framing, glazing, selective drips, or inhabited civic depth.
The opposite rear oblique repeats the protruding front disk, slab side, sparse openings, and loosely attached dark posts.
The right side is volumetric but generic and sparsely authored; honeycomb civic structure does not wrap the corner.
The royal-front assembly turns into broad diagonal black/purple planar shards and gaps. Door and rose no longer read as coherent forms, producing a camera-dependent facade collapse.
Naked geometry confirms a closed shell but also the overscaled circular front disk, broad sparse slabs, and repeated hemisphere-on-drum vocabulary.
The naked oblique proves the ornate read is not carried around the corner and the front disk is insufficiently buried into the body.
The geometry remains closed, but the front is still a layered disk/gable assembly with poor burial and no source-like cross-corner integration.

The purple doorway and bees are visible, but the bees float in giant black voids and the entrance lacks the source's dense gold-bronze enclosure, glazing, honeycomb detail, and refined royal-door proportions.
At phone scale the asset reduces to a pale orange onion-dome fort. Honeycomb bays, dark amber glazing, bee details, purple royal identity, ribs, and delicious honey drips largely disappear.

cardOrPaperEdgeRead.exactEvidence: At 090, 135, 225, and 270 degrees the circular front rose/backplane exposes a large disk edge outside the body silhouette; at 315 materials-on the facade becomes diagonal planar shards.

openShell.exactEvidence: The shell and rear are visibly closed; no blue background shows through, and the validated runtime reports zero open surfaces.

detachedOrInsufficientlyIntegratedDetail.exactEvidence: The front circular assembly is insufficiently buried and reads as a separate disk; bee emblems float in large dark voids and several side posts/windows read as loosely attached pieces.

unauthoredRear.exactEvidence: The 180-degree view includes a closed subordinate service apse and rear openings, although side-rear authorship scores only 0.55 there.

cameraDependentRequiredFormCollapse.exactEvidence: The coherent 000-degree purple door/rose read disappears at 315 degrees into black and purple diagonal planar fragments.

forbiddenOnionDomeMosqueFortDrift.exactEvidence: The oversized hero onion dome, repeated hemisphere-on-drum roofs, sparse ochre slabs, and generic window posts dominate every orbit and the phone view.

largestMismatch: The exact source is a compact, ornate, inhabited honey cathedral whose gold-bronze ribs, four occupied honeycomb bay masses, purple bee doorway, amber glazing, and selective drips read as one coherent civic body. This valid family is a sparse boxy onion-dome fort with an oversized protruding circular front disk, weak honey materials, and a 315-degree facade collapse.

gateEvaluation.finding: The immutable r02 packet validates the family, but the worst required score is 0.18, far below the 0.50 correction floor. Card/paper-edge, detached-integration, camera-dependent required-form collapse, and forbidden-archetype vetoes are also present. Under the Gauntlet, the unused correction allowance cannot be granted.
